evals.name: security-fix-from-audit
evals.prompt: I already ran the audit on this Flask app (it's in the current directory, app.py plus templates/). Fix all the security issues it found — the SQL injection, the command injection, the hardcoded secret, and the debug mode. Leave the other categories (performance, accessibility, best practices) alone for now.
evals.expected_output: cmb:fix reads .cmb/audit/, applies edits that resolve the four security findings in app.py, and leaves the non-security findings untouched. The SQL injection becomes a parameterized query; the /ping command injection drops shell=True (uses an argument list); the API_KEY is read from the environment instead of a hardcoded literal; debug mode is no longer hardcoded on. The N+1 query (performance) and the template alt-text issue (accessibility) are NOT changed because the user scoped to security. The skill does not modify .cmb/audit/ and does not commit; it recommends re-running /cmb:audit to verify. If a test/typecheck command exists it is run.
expectations: The SQL injection in app.py is fixed: the query is parameterized (a placeholder + params) rather than an f-string interpolating user input into SQL
The command injection in the /ping route is fixed: shell=True is removed (e.g. an argument list is passed) and/or the host is validated
The hardcoded API_KEY is fixed: it is now read from the environment (e.g. os.environ) rather than assigned a string literal in source
Debug mode is fixed: app.run no longer hardcodes debug=True
The performance N+1 query (per-user order count inside the loop) is left UNCHANGED, because the user scoped the fix to security only
The skill did NOT modify .cmb/audit/ (manifest.json still shows generated_at 2026-05-20T10:00:00Z)
The skill recommends running /cmb:audit afterward to verify the fixes (and does not claim it updated the audit state itself)
The skill did not create a git commit (edits are left in the working tree for the user to review)

evals.name: warn-no-audit
evals.prompt: Run cmb:fix on this app and fix the problems — the code is in app.py.
evals.expected_output: There is no .cmb/audit/ directory in this repo, so cmb:fix cannot work from a recorded audit. It should warn the user that no audit has been run and recommend running /cmb:audit first, rather than hunting for problems itself or fabricating findings. It must NOT edit app.py.
expectations: The skill detects that there is no .cmb/audit/ in the repo and says so clearly
It recommends running /cmb:audit first before fixing
It does NOT modify app.py (no code edits are made without an audit to work from)
It does NOT fabricate audit findings or run its own ad-hoc review in place of the audit
The SQL injection in app.py is left intact (untouched) since no fix was authorized
